record.paper_title: Observational Cosmology: caveats and open questions in the standard model
record.original_question: Are high-redshift quasars, or quasi-stellar objects, physically associated with and possibly ejected from nearby low-redshift active galaxies, with intrinsic or quantized redshift components, rather than lying at the large cosmological distances implied by their observed redshifts?

evidence.quote: Non-orthodox hypothesis shared by very few astronomers (Arp, Burbidge & Burbidge and few others) claim that QSOs are being ejected by low redshift active galaxies.
The main idea in any case is that QSOs are really at the same distance than nearby galaxies in spite of their high redshifts.
Detailed investigations of several QSO-galaxy pairs show that the galaxy and QSO are apparently connected.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Quasi-stellar objects (QSOs), commonly called quasars, are compact extragalactic sources whose optical spectra exhibit large redshifts z. Under the standard cosmological interpretation, these redshifts arise from the expansion of the Universe (Hubble flow), placing the QSOs at large cosmological distances. An alternative, non-standard hypothesis asserts that a significant population of high-redshift QSOs is physically associated with, and possibly has been ejected from, nearby low-redshift active galaxies, so that the QSOs lie at essentially the same distance as those host galaxies. Under this hypothesis a substantial part of an observed QSO redshift would be non-cosmological in origin, having an intrinsic component (for example, a discrete or "quantized" contribution depending only on the source), rather than being due to recessional motion.

Determine whether such physical QSO–galaxy associations exist as a generic phenomenon: that is, decide whether high-redshift QSOs found in apparent proximity (including cases showing morphological bridges or filamentary connections) to low-redshift active galaxies are genuinely physically associated with those galaxies and carry intrinsic/non-cosmological redshift components, or whether all such configurations are chance projections of background QSOs whose redshifts are purely cosmological.
artifact.status_search_result: The mainstream astronomical community has firmly concluded that quasar redshifts are cosmological in origin, placing QSOs at large distances. Apparent QSO–galaxy proximities are interpreted as chance projections; statistical tests have found no evidence of the predicted periodicity in log(1+z) or of intrinsic-redshift components. The ejection/intrinsic-redshift hypothesis of Arp, Burbidge and collaborators is regarded as refuted by the standard model and supported by only a small minority.

status_evidence.title: Halton Arp - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The rest of the community regards these as chance alignments... Arp's hypothesis has very few supporters.
status_evidence.claim: Scientific consensus rejects the intrinsic-redshift / QSO-ejection hypothesis.

status_evidence.title: Galaxies and the Universe - Alternate Approaches and the Redshift Controversy
status_evidence.snippet: Tests for periodicity in log(1+z) found no significant signal at the predicted frequency.
status_evidence.claim: Predicted quantized/intrinsic redshift signatures are not seen in modern data.

status_evidence.title: Apparent discordant redshift QSO-galaxy associations
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of discordant redshift associations as a marginal viewpoint.
status_evidence.claim: Discordant redshift claims remain a fringe position in the literature.
